subject: DPA clarifications — controller/processor; subprocessors; breach notice
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme-payments.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@acme-payments.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + DPA clarifications

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the deep dive into Acme's integration and compliance requirements. As discussed, I'm summarizing the open questions your legal/procurement team asked so we can get you definitive answers from our security & legal teams. Attached is a short DPA summary that maps our standard positions to common asks.

Key items from the call (please confirm I captured these):
- Controller vs Processor: You want confirmation that Redwood will be the Processor for data sent to the inference API and that Acme will remain the Controller.
- Subprocessors: A current list + process for advance notice of new subprocessors.
- Breach notice SLA: request for 72-hour notification for incidents involving Acme data.
- Data residency: Requirement that all inference data for EU customers remain in EU (option to discuss Private deployment).
- Data retention & deletion: How long PII/inputs/outputs and logs are retained by default; ability to purge on contract termination.
- Logging/audit controls: What audit logs we can provide (access, API calls, user-level logs) and retention windows.

Next steps from Redwood: I'll loop in Security and Legal to confirm our standard positions and any exceptions we can offer. Can you confirm whether procurement would accept our standard DPA with those points clarified, or if they will propose redlines up front? Also let me know the procurement contact's preferred file format for the subprocessor list (CSV/PDF).

I'll follow up once I have confirmation from our internal teams — targeting EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0189

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + DPA clarifications

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect and captures things well. A few clarifying questions from procurement/legal so we can move this to our contract review: 

1) Can you confirm in writing whether Redwood will sign as Processor only, or if Redwood requires any Controller obligations in the DPA? Our standard approach is Controller/Processor separation.
2) For subprocessors: we need a current list plus commitment to provide notice within 30 days of adding a subprocessor (or a mechanism to object).
3) Breach notice: we typically request a 72-hour notification for incidents materially affecting our data. Will Redwood accept that?
4) Data deletion: request that customer data (inputs/outputs/PII) be deleted within 30 days of termination or upon written request. Is that supported for hosted customers?
5) Data residency: for EU customers we require EU data residency; if Redwood can't guarantee hosted residency, what are the options (e.g., Private deployment, dedicated region)?
6) Audit artifacts: Can you provide SOC 2 Type II report and a sample subprocessor list? Prefer PDF/CSV.

If you can loop legal/security with proposed language for the DPA items above, that will speed procurement review. Thanks — Alicia

Alicia Gomez
Head of Procurement | Acme Payments
alicia.gomez@acme-payments.com

Hi team — looping Legal (Vivek) and Security (Dev) on Acme's procurement questions. Key asks from their list are below — please see the attached DPA summary and subprocessor stub. Acme is a mid-market payments processor; deal is ramping quickly and procurement wants answers before sending redlines.

Acme asks to confirm:
- Our role: Processor-only vs any Controller obligations (they expect Processor).
- Subprocessors: current list + 30-day notice / objection mechanism.
- Breach notice: 72-hour notification requirement.
- Deletion: purge customer data within 30 days of termination/on request (hosted customers).
- Data residency: EU residency requirement for EU business; options: Private deployment or dedicated region?
- Audit artifacts: SOC2 Type II + subprocessor CSV.

Suggested quick answers to speed things along (please edit):
- We operate as Processor for customer-supplied inference data; customers are Controllers. We'll sign a Processor DPA.
- We publish an up-to-date subprocessor list and can provide CSV. Standard notice is 30 days for material additions; we can include an objection process.
- Our standard breach notification SLA is 72 hours for incidents impacting customer data; confirm exceptions for legal obligations.
- For hosted customers, default retention windows: inputs/outputs 30 days, operational logs 90 days; we can negotiate for longer/shorter retention or offer Private deployment for stricter residency.
- Data residency: we offer region pinning (EU region) and a Private deployment option for strict residency/on-prem.
- SOC2 and subprocessor list: available via secure link/attachment.

Can you confirm canonical language we should send back to Acme procurement? If changes required, please highlight. They prefer PDF/CSV attachments for artifacts.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Summary.pdf, subprocessors_list.csv

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA clarifications - Acme Payments (procurement asks)

Marissa — thanks for the summary. Below are our standard positions and suggested language you can send to Acme. I've attached the latest SOC 2 Type II stub and the current subprocessor CSV (redacted where needed).

1) Controller vs Processor
Standard position: Redwood operates as a Processor for inference requests and related telemetry. Customers are Controllers with respect to the data they provide to our service. We are willing to execute a Processor-only DPA. Recommended sentence for DPA: "Redwood Inference will act as Processor on behalf of Customer for the processing activities described in Appendix A; Customer is the Controller of Customer Data."

2) Subprocessors
Standard position: We maintain a published list of subprocessors and provide notice of material additions. Recommended approach: provide current CSV and commit to 30 days' notice for new subprocessors; include an objection process for lawful reasons. Link/attachment: subprocessors_list.csv.

3) Breach notice
Standard position: Redwood will provide notice of confirmed security incidents affecting Customer Data within 72 hours of confirmation. Exceptions: if legal restrictions (e.g., law enforcement) preclude notice, we will provide notice as permitted. Recommended clause: "Processor will notify Controller without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours after becoming aware of a security incident affecting Controller Data."

4) Data deletion & retention
Standard position for hosted customers: default retention windows: inputs/outputs (30 days), operational logs (90 days). We support contractual changes: commit to delete Customer Data within 30 days following termination upon Controller's request (subject to legal holds). For EU residency customers requiring strict controls, recommend Private deployment or a dedicated region addendum.

5) Data residency
We support region pinning for hosted customers and offer Private (customer-managed) deployments or on-prem packages for strict residency requirements. Provide a short note that Private deployments require separate commercial/legal arrangements.

6) Audit artifacts
We can provide SOC 2 Type II report and the subprocessor CSV via secure link/attachment. Provide links in the email and note that full SOC artifacts require an NDA/secure access.

Next steps: You can send the summary below directly to Acme procurement with the attachments (SOC2 stub + subprocessors CSV). If Acme returns redlines to the DPA, please forward them to legal (me) for review. If they request alternative breach timelines or deletion windows, escalate — some exceptions need leadership approval.

Let me know if you'd like me to draft a short DPA amendment.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
General Counsel | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
